content.text:
I submitted index 30 (Ni 0.17 / Sb 0.83) as the best composition. At 1.08% EQE it was the highest of the three I could measure. All three merit measurements are used; I did not use any XRD.

| Index | Ni / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.34 / 0.66 (NiSb2O6) | 0.015 |
| 27 | 0.21 / 0.79 | 0.047 |
| 30 | 0.17 / 0.83 | 1.08 |

- **Starting point:** I measured index 21 first because the MACE model puts the NiSb2O6 phase on the stability hull. It was the stable choice, but it performed badly. I ignored MEGNet's 0.04 eV band-gap prediction for this phase because it doesn't look physical for a nickel oxide.
- **Sb-rich end:** index 30, at the Sb-rich edge of the library, was about 70 times better than index 21.
- **Last measurement:** index 27 read only 0.047%, so there is no hidden peak between 21 and 30. EQE jumps sharply right at the edge.

**Untested:**
- **The Ni-rich half (Sb below 0.5):** I didn't measure it at all, even though the automated suggestion tool pointed to index 0. That end is mostly nickel oxide, which absorbs poorly at these photon energies and generally makes a poor photoanode. So I judged it unlikely to beat index 30, but I haven't confirmed that.
- **Indices 28 and 29:** they sit between 27 and 30 and weren't measured, so a small gain there can't be ruled out.
